title: Yield Point: Definition, Formula, and Examples
summary: The yield point is a mechanical property that represents the transition between elastic and plastic deformation. Learn more about it here.
body_text: Why Do Plastics Often Lack a Sharp Yield Point? Plastics often lack a sharp yield point because the molecular structure consists of long-chain molecules that untangle gradually under stress. Thermoplastics (nylon) experience a slow transition from elastic stretching to permanent sliding. The internal arrangement lacks the rigid crystalline lattice found in structural metals. Molecular chains slide past one another over a wide range of stress levels. Viscoelastic properties cause the material to respond differently depending on the rate of loading. Temperature impacts the clarity of the deformation threshold. Rapid cooling during manufacturing creates a different response than slow cooling. Laboratory tests show a continuous curve, making the definition of a single point difficult. Designers observe the gradual shift in slope on the stress-strain diagram. The absence of a sharp break necessitates alternative measurement techniques. Standardized tests help determine the functional limits of the material. Engineering applications require a predictable threshold to prevent failure in plastic parts. Structural response remains sensitive to environmental conditions (humidity). The mechanical behavior remains complex due to the nature of polymers. Stress-strain curves for the materials remain nonlinear. Engineers use offset methods instead. Are Yield-Based Design Rules Still Used for Plastics? Yes, yield-based design rules apply to plastics, but require numerous modifications to account for unique material behaviors. Engineers apply safety factors to the observed yield stress during the selection of materials (polycarbonate). Calculations include the impact of long-term loading on the stability of the part. Plastic components experience time-dependent deformation, known as creep, even under constant stress levels below the initial yield point. Environmental factors (temperature) require adjustments to the standard design formulas. Performance criteria differ from those applied to structural steel. Designers analyze the relationship between stress and strain over extended periods. Industry standards provide guidelines for using yield strength in thermoplastic applications. Structural integrity remains a priority in the manufacturing of consumer goods. High-temperature environments accelerate the loss of structural rigidity. Engineers combine yield data with other mechanical properties to ensure durability. The application of the rules prevents sudden failure in load-bearing structures. Safety protocols dictate the limits of acceptable deformation. Long-term loads trigger the phenomenon of Creep. How Is Yield Point Shown on Engineering Stress-Strain Curves? The yield point is shown on engineering stress-strain curves as a marked shift from the linear region to the curved region. The first segment of the graph signifies the elastic region where stress remains proportional to strain. A clear deviation from the straight line indicates the onset of permanent deformation. Metals (annealed mild steel) often display a yield point plateau during the yielding process. This plateau signifies that the material continues to elongate at a relatively constant stress level. Visual representation allows engineers to identify the maximum load for elastic operation. Data points from the tensile test create the graphical profile. The slope change signifies the movement of atoms into new equilibrium positions. Measuring the coordinates provides the specific yield strength of the material. Graphical software highlights the transition to assist in the analysis of material performance. Structural design relies on the clarity of the diagram. The pattern remains unique to each material category. Observations confirm the end of temporary bond stretching. The yield point appears as a marked transition from the linear to the curved region. Structural steel displays a flat plateau. Visual aids help engineers identify yielding. What Is the Difference Between Engineering and True Yield Point? The difference between the engineering yield point and the true yield point exists in the specific cross-sectional area used for the stress calculation. Engineering stress calculations utilize the initial dimensions of the specimen measured before the test. The method ignores the reduction in width as the material stretches. True stress calculations account for the instantaneous cross-sectional area at every point during the deformation. The values remain nearly identical during the initial elastic phase because dimensional changes remain negligible. Discrepancy increases once the material enters the plastic region. The true stress-strain curve deviates significantly from the engineering curve after yielding, as the true stress accounts for the decreasing cross-sectional area. Engineers prefer the simpler version for practical design tasks in construction. Research scientists utilize the more accurate version to understand the fundamental physics of the material. Software simulations require accurate data to predict behavior near the failure point. Manufacturing processes (rolling) rely on true stress values. The choice of the measurement method depends on the required level of precision. Engineering yield calculations rely on the original area, while accuracy in true stress requires the actual area. Engineering values are practical for design. Is True Yield Strength Used in Practical Design? No, true yield strength is not used in practical engineering design. Engineering yield strength serves as the standard (bridges). Designers use the initial cross-sectional area to determine load limits. Practical applications ignore the reduction in area. Engineering values provide a standardized and practical approach for design, as most structures are intended to operate within the elastic region where the difference between engineering and true stress is negligible. Design codes (AISC) specify yield values. True stress-strain data remains confined to advanced academic studies. Research scientists investigate the fundamental mechanics of metal. Material failure analysis requires true stress data. Engineering stress defines the force divided by the original area. Simple calculations aid the design of 1,000,000s of components. Accuracy remains sufficient, as structural integrity depends on maintaining stress levels below the engineering yield point. True stress defines the actual internal force per unit area. Theoretical models benefit from true stress inputs. Practical engineering remains focused on standard testing results. Structural codes use engineering values to ensure long-term stability. Reliability in construction originates from standardized engineering yield strength. Standards ensure safety in buildings. Engineers calculate the required thickness of plates. Each component withstands the expected load. Accuracy in measurements leads to successful projects. Professional guidelines emphasize the use of engineering stress. Stability depends on the properties of the material. Technical manuals provide the necessary data. Standardized procedures eliminate confusion in the design phase. Engineering yield strength remains the primary metric. What Are Common Yield Point Examples? The common yield point examples are listed below. Steel : Steel exhibits a high yield point due to its strong atomic bonds and tightly packed crystalline structure. This makes it suitable for applications requiring high strength, such as construction and automotive industries. Aluminum : Aluminum has a lower yield point compared to steel because of its more flexible atomic structure. It is commonly used in lightweight applications, such as aircraft and packaging, where strength is less critical. Mild Steel : Mild steel is a common example of a material with a distinct, sharp yield point. This behavior is caused by interstitial carbon atoms pinning dislocations, a phenomenon characteristic of low-carbon ferritic steels used in structural applications. Copper : Copper has a relatively low yield point and is highly ductile. It is used in electrical wiring and plumbing where high conductivity and formability are more critical than high yield strength. It is used in electrical wiring and plumbing where high conductivity is more critical than strength. Titanium : Titanium exhibits a high yield point, making it ideal for aerospace applications. It combines strength with lightness and resistance to corrosion, which is why it is used in aircraft and medical implants. Polycarbonate Plastic : Polycarbonate is an example of a plastic material with a moderate yield point. Polycarbonate is known for its toughness and impact resistance, making it suitable for applications like eyewear lenses and protective covers. How Does Yield Point Differ in Steel? Yield point differs in steel compared to polymers in several key ways. Steel (mild steel) displays a sharp yield point, marking the moment pinned dislocations break free from Cottrell atmospheres to initiate macroscopic plastic flow. The distinct transition makes it easier to identify safety limits, as steel maintains a predictable linear region before yielding. Polymers experience a smooth transition into the plastic range, with molecular chains untangling over a broad range of stress values, leading to gradual deformation. Sharp yield points in steel simplify the determination of functional limits, while polymers require the offset method to establish a functional yield point due to their nonlinear behavior early in the loading process. The clear yield plateau in steel is vital for structural engineers, who rely on this to ensure material safety and predict performance. Material selection depends on the required rigidity of the final product, with steel offering more predictable behavior under stress. Understanding the differences between steel metal , and polymers helps improve the accuracy of structural simulations and component design. Is Steel’s Yield Point Higher Than Aluminum’s? Yes, Steel’s yield point is higher than the yield point of aluminum. Standard structural steel has a yield strength of 250 MPa (A36 steel). High-strength steels reach values exceeding 500 MPa. Aluminum alloys provide lower resistance to permanent deformation. The yield strength in common aluminum (6061-T6) ranges from 150 to 300 MPa. Steel offers superior load-bearing capabilities in heavy construction. Aluminum remains the preferred choice in applications where weight reduction is a priority (aircraft). The density of steel is nearly three times higher than the density of aluminum. Weight penalties limit the use of steel in portable electronics. Strength-to-weight ratios favor aluminum in specific engineering contexts. Designers compensate for lower yield strength by increasing the thickness of the material. Structural members in skyscrapers rely on the extreme strength of steel. Aerospace engineers accept the lower strength to improve fuel efficiency. Reliability in automotive frames depends on the high-yield point of specialized steel. Weight differences explain why aluminum is lighter yet weaker. Modern manufacturing utilizes the properties of Aluminum Alloy . How Does the Yield Point Affect Injection Molding Processes? The yield point affects the injection molding process by determining the safe operating pressures in the machinery. Designers set pressure limits to ensure the mold remains in the elastic region. Exceeding the yield point causes permanent deformation of the tool steel. Damaged molds produce defective parts. Structural integrity of the mold plates depends on the yield threshold. Clamping forces reach high levels during the injection of molten plastic. Stress distribution analysis prevents localized yielding in thin mold sections. High-strength materials reduce the risk of structural failure. Maintenance schedules include checks identifying signs of permanent set. Engineering calculations define the maximum allowable cavity pressure. Safe processing requires a thorough understanding of material properties. Injection molding machines use sensors to monitor the force applied to the mold. Precision in manufacturing originates from proper material selection. Selecting the correct steel grade prevents costly repairs. Improvement of the process relies on the mechanics of Injection Molding . Why Is Yield Point Critical During Injection Molding of Plastics? The yield point of the solidified plastic is critical because if the injection and packing pressures create internal residual stresses that exceed the material's yield strength after cooling, the part may warp or fail. Yield strength serves as a key guide for selecting the appropriate material, ensuring that the plastic withstands the molding process without experiencing irreversible deformation. Materials with higher yield points are less likely to be affected by the significant pressures used in injection molding. Engineers prevent issues such as warping and structural failure during the molding process by choosing materials with an appropriate yield point. The yield point helps to ensure that the molded parts retain their intended shape and functionality throughout the production cycle, leading to high-quality finished products. Can Injection Molding Forces Exceed a Material’s Yield Point? Yes, injection molding forces can exceed a material's yield point if the design is poorly executed. Excessive pressure or improper molding parameters can cause the material to deform permanently, resulting in warping, cracking, or even failure of the molded parts. The risk is heightened if the material is not appropriately selected for the required molding process or if the mold design does not account for the material's yield strength. Proper design and engineering are essential to avoid this issue. Manufacturers prevent the forces from exceeding the material’s yield point, ensuring that the plastic parts maintain their intended shape and strength by carefully controlling the injection pressure, temperature, and material selection. How Does Yield Point Differ Between 6061 and 7075 Aluminum? The yield point differs between 6061 and 7075 aluminum alloys. 7075 aluminum has a much higher yield point than 6061, making it stronger and more resistant to deformation under stress. The increased strength makes 7075 ideal for applications requiring high strength, such as aerospace and military structures. It comes at the cost of ductility, as 7075 is less flexible and more prone to brittle failure under certain conditions. 6061 aluminum is easier to machine and weld, making it a more versatile choice for general manufacturing and construction. It maintains a good balance of strength, ductility, and workability, making it suitable for a wide range of structural applications, although it has a lower yield point. The differences in yield points and material properties highlight the importance of selecting the appropriate alloy based on the specific requirements of a project, when considering strength versus machinability. The 6061 Aluminum Alloy is favored for its versatility and ease of fabrication. What Causes the Yield Strength Difference Between 6061 and 7075 Aluminum? The yield strength difference between 6061 and 7075 aluminum is caused by the distinct alloying elements and heat treatments used in each. 7075 aluminum contains a higher amount of zinc, which allows for the formation of fine precipitates (MgZn2) through heat treatment, significantly increasing strength via precipitation hardening. It makes 7075 aluminum alloy ideal for applications where high strength is critical, such as in aerospace and military sectors. 6061 aluminum contains magnesium and silicon, which form Mg2Si precipitates during heat treatment, providing a balance of strength, ductility, and workability. The alloying elements in 6061 offer a good mix of properties, making it easier to machine and weld, though it results in a lower yield strength compared to 7075. The heat treatment processes applied to both alloys further influence their respective yield strengths, with 7075 undergoing more intensive heat treatment to achieve its higher strength. The 7075 Aluminum Alloy is more suitable for applications where high tensile strength is required, but the 6061 Aluminum Alloy offers better versatility in terms of fabrication and processing. Does 7075 Aluminum Have a Higher Yield Point Than 6061 Aluminum? Yes, 7075 aluminum has a significantly higher yield point than 6061 aluminum. The typical yield strength of 7075 aluminum is about 500 MPa, making it much stronger and more resistant to deformation than 6061 aluminum, which has a yield strength of around 275 MPa. The higher yield strength of 7075 is due to its alloying elements, particularly zinc, which improve its structural integrity. It makes 7075 aluminum a better choice for high-stress applications where strength is a priority, while 6061 is more commonly used in applications requiring a good balance of strength and workability.

These free radicals then cause oxidative stress, since the unstable structure of these molecules makes them more prone to oxidation (this is the same process that causes a cut apple to turn brown) [3]. Antioxidants can prevent and reverse the damage caused by free radicals by lending these unstable molecules an electron. Simply put, this helpful addition makes it harder for a free radical to continue to damage your skin cells. By incorporating antioxidants into your skincare regimen, then, you’re protecting your skin cells from the damage caused by oxidative stress—which helps you maintain healthy skin. What Are the Benefits of Antioxidants for Your Skin? By fighting the effects of free radicals and exposure to oxidative stress, antioxidants can benefit your skin in a number of ways. From reducing the signs of aging to maintaining a smooth, uniform complexion, integrating this powerful component into your skincare routine can help your skin look and feel its best. Free radicals from sun exposure can also cause changes in the production of melanin in the skin, which can trigger the appearance of dark spots and dull or uneven skin tone. Antioxidants can soothe the skin and combat inflammation by defending against the effects of free radicals in the body, working to reduce the photodamage that occurs when ultraviolet (UV) rays meet unprotected skin. As a result, antioxidants have the potential ability to quell inflammatory symptoms like skin redness to facilitate an overall more even skin tone. #2 Improving Signs of Premature Aging By damaging the tissues and cells in your body, prolonged exposure to oxidative stress can begin to make the skin look duller and cause the development of premature aging, including fine lines and wrinkles. Fortunately, antioxidants can halt and reverse these processes, helping the skin regain its glow by protecting against factors that cause extrinsic again, like sun exposure, pollution, and smoking, or vaping [5]. #3 Protecting Skin from Sun Damage Chronic sun exposure is a common culprit of free radical development as well as the development of oxidative stress, so it’s important to combat UV damage by integrating antioxidants into your skincare routine. Since antioxidants contain anti-inflammatory properties, they help calm the skin and protect against UV rays when used alongside sunscreen. When antioxidants reduce inflammation, they allow healthy cells to develop, which contributes to your healthiest skin. Besides combating inflammation, some antioxidants, like vitamin C , can also boost collagen production. Collagen is a protein that the body produces naturally, but oxidative stress can halt its production, which can negatively impact the elasticity and appearance of the skin [6]. Learning how to increase collagen in your skin can aid your anti-aging efforts, regardless of your age. Eating foods high in antioxidants and applying products topically that contain them can help to restore the appearance of the skin by reversing the damage caused by sun exposure and free radicals. #5 Preventing the Development of Skin Conditions Studies have found that the topical application and ingestion of antioxidants, like vitamin E, can also prevent the development of various skin conditions, like acne or atopic dermatitis [7]. Since these diseases occur because of inflammation in the body, products with anti-inflammatory ingredients, including antioxidants, may be able to slow their development. Other conditions, like psoriasis, are a result of oxidative stress, meaning that compounds like antioxidants may help to rid the body of free radicals and stop the development of new ones [8]. Once you have the latest version of the CLI installed, you can run the following command: depot configure-docker Successfully installed Depot as a Docker CLI plugin Behind the scenes, in addition to installing Depot as a Docker CLI plugin, the command configures a default buildx driver that routes builds to Depot. Allowing any docker buildx build commands to use Depot, in addition to the existing docker build command. Using Depot with Docker Compose Once the configure-docker command is executed, you can use Depot with Docker Compose without changing a single line of code. All you need to do is ensure you have a Depot project configured for your build. You can do this via: Setting a DEPOT_PROJECT_ID environment variable to the project ID of the project you want to use for builds. Running depot init in the root of the repository in which you're building your image. The command creates a depot.json file that our plugin will detect. If you have a Depot project configured, you can run docker compose build , and Depot will build the images in your Docker compose file. You can see this in action in the following example. Here is our example Docker compose file with a single service: services : app : build : dockerfile : Dockerfile.app platforms : - 'linux/amd64' - 'linux/arm64' tags : - repo/app:123 The Dockerfile that it is building looks like this: FROM node:16 AS build WORKDIR /app COPY package.json yarn.lock tsconfig.json ./ COPY src/ ./src/ RUN yarn install --immutable RUN yarn build FROM node:16 WORKDIR /app COPY --from=build /app/node_modules /app/node_modules COPY --from=build /app/dist /app/dist COPY gifs-to-upload/ dist/gifs-to-upload/ ENV NODE_ENV production CMD [ "node" , "--enable-source-maps" , "./dist/index.js" ] Now, all you have to do is call build or up just as you usually would. docker compose build #1 [app depot] build: https://depot.dev/orgs/123/projects/456/builds/000 #1 DONE 0.0s #2 [app depot] build: https://depot.dev/orgs/123/projects/456/builds/111 #2 DONE 0.0s # ...continued output from Docker Compose You can see that the Docker is building with Depot. It creates a separate build for each architecture and service defined in the compose.yml . If you want to use Depot with Docker Compose but prefer to use the up command, you can also do that. Just run docker compose up , and Depot will build your images. docker compose up [+] Building 33.0s ( 19/19 ) = > [app depot] build: https://depot.dev/orgs/123/projects/456/builds/222 0.0s = > [app depot] launching arm64 machine 2.0s = > [app depot] connecting to arm64 machine 6.9s = > [app internal] load build definition from Dockerfile.app = > ...continued output from Docker Compose Note on Docker Compose Docker Compose creates a new build for each service and architecture defined in the compose.yml . If you have a docker-compose.yml that defines 3 services, and you're building for 2 architectures, you will have 6 builds created in Depot. Power of Depot for all tools We've got a lot of requests to integrate Depot with other developer tools out there that need to build containers on demand. Tools like Dev Containers and goreleaser are great examples of this. Before this command, these tools couldn't integrate with Depot. They call docker build or docker buildx build directly, and there was no way to configure them to use a different builder. Now, with depot configure-docker , all tools using Docker or buildx internally can route their image builds to Depot. We have an integration guide and documentation for how this works with Dev Containers and docker build and docker buildx build in general . We're excited about what this new command will unlock for folks! We will put out some new integration guides for other tools that need to build a Docker container on demand, so stay tuned for those. You can also hop in our Community Discord and let us know which tools you'd like us to integrate with next! title: How to Use Plivo’s SMS API with ChatGPT
summary: ChatGPT for messaging: Learn how to integrate Plivo's SMS API with ChatGPT. Unleash the power of AI-driven messaging & enhance your customer communication with Plivo’s SMS API.
body_text: Have you jumped on the ChatGPT bandwagon yet? We’ve been brainstorming how OpenAI’s AI-adjacent natural language processing tool might help Plivo customers. Ideas have ranged from applications as simple as a natural language autoresponder to an application that runs a script based on voice or SMS input to a more complex use case such as an SMS chatbot emulation. (We’d be interested in hearing about anything you’ve already built, or that you’re thinking about.) Plivo and ChatGPT can interact in two ways - think of them as “to” and “from.” A Plivo action (such as an incoming call or text message) could be a trigger to invoke ChatGPT. For instance, someone might text a question with an #askChatGPT hashtag. Plivo could use ChatGPT APIs to pass that query to ChatGPT and return the answer to the person who initiated the query. Another use case, for data going in the other direction, would have someone invoke something from ChatGPT that triggers a Plivo action. For instance, you could go to the OpenAI’s Playground page and ask ChatGPT to text everyone in a list a weather report for their area. ChatGPT can’t use Plivo APIs to call Plivo directly. Any application that wants to allow ChatGPT to use its APIs has to write an OpenAI plugin - and plugins are just leaking out in beta form, so a Plivo plugin won’t be available by the time you read this. However, Plivo partners with Zapier , an application integration tool, and Zapier is developing a plugin for ChatGPT that lets Playground users call zaps - and it’s easy to write a zap that triggers a Plivo action . How well can three very different platforms work together? We thought a post that walks you through how to send messages through Plivo to ChatGPT, and from ChatGPT to recipients via Plivo, would be valuable. We start with having a Plivo action invoke ChatGPT. → From Plivo to ChatGPT in code → To see how a Plivo action could trigger ChatGPT, we wanted to write a little proof-of-concept code that takes the text of any SMS message that comes in on a specific number, calls OpenAI’s API with that text, and replies to the SMS with ChatGPT’s answer. And in the spirit of keeping things simple, we thought we’d give ChatGPT a chance to write the code for us. We gave it a prompt: Using the Plivo Python SDK, write Python code to send the text of an incoming SMS message to ChatGPT and return the reply from ChatGPT to the number that sent the first text. And it returned this code. .highlight pre{ background-color: rgb(33, 33, 48); border-radius: 0; padding: 15px 18px 15px 18px; } pre.lineno{ color: #fff; opacity: .3; } .w-richtext figure { max-width: 100%; position: relative; } # Import Plivo and ChatGPT import plivo from chatgpt import ChatGPT # Create an instance of ChatGPT chatgpt = ChatGPT() # Define function to process incoming message, send to ChatGPT, and return response def process_incoming_message(incoming_message, incoming_number): # Send incoming message to ChatGPT chatgpt_response = chatgpt.send_text(incoming_message) # Send response from ChatGPT back to sender client = plivo.RestClient() client.messages.create( src='', dst=incoming_number, text=chatgpt_response ) ‍ That’s a decent starting point, but ChatGPT isn’t going to take any developers’ jobs just yet. It’s a very simple use case - but sometimes that’s all you need. However, in this case, one fatal flaw is the lack of a ChatGPT module with APIs that let you make queries. Plivo CTO Mike Ricordeau took the concept and made it scalable. His sms_bot.py code, using Python and Flask, is available online, so you can clone it and play with it. Follow the instructions in the README file. Before you deploy the application, you must expose it at a public URL. To do that, we recommend using ngrok. Make sure to specify to ngrok the same port on which the sms_bot.py application is running. Ngrok will return a forwarding IP address you can use. Once you’ve obtained a forwarding address from ngrok, visit the Plivo console and add a Plivo application. Specify the address, postpended with “/sms,” for the Message URL. Next, pick one of your active phone numbers and associate it with the application you just created. In the Application Type drop-down, choose XML Application, and under Plivo Application choose the name of the Plivo application you added. Now the application should be live and available. You can try it by texting a message to the phone number you used. Plivo should receive the question and POST the request to the Message URL, and ngrok forwards it to the Python application, which connects to OpenAI and asks the question. OpenAI gives the answer. The Python application then returns a Message XML element with the response, which is sent to the user’s phone number. The entire “transaction” took about four seconds from when I tapped Send to when I received a response. ← To Plivo from ChatGPT via Zapier ← Suppose, instead, you want to have ChatGPT call Plivo to send a text message. As we said, ChatGPT can’t use Plivo APIs directly. Fortunately, Plivo partner Zapier is a member of the OpenAI ChatGPT plugin program. As we mentioned, Zapier is an application integration tool that lets anyone connect disparate web applications together in a workflow. Anyone with a ChatGPT Plus account can use Zapier to perform an action from ChatGPT that calls Plivo. To try it out for SMS API integration you first have to set things up. Sign up for a ChatGPT Plus subscription - it costs $20 a month - and you’ll need a Zapier account too. From the ChatGPT home screen click on your account name in the bottom left corner, then Settings > Data Controls, and enable 2FA. The page displays a QR code that you have to scan with an authenticator application running on a smartphone. The app should display a six-digit number for you to copy into the authentication dialog. Once you’ve enabled 2FA, click on GPT-4 at the top of the ChatGPT home screen and choose Plugins from the drop-down menu. From the Plug-in store, find Zapier and click Install . Your browser will open a new window and Zapier will prompt you to connect; click Allow . After you’ve enabled the Zapier plugin you can go back to the main ChatGPT window and ask a question. When you have an answer, you can say something like “Send that via Zapier and Plivo.” The first time you do that, ChatGPT will give you a link to click on that brings up a page where to enable an action. We’ve written documentation on how to use Zapier with Plivo , sans ChatGPT; it talks about the available options. If you’re one of those free spirits who prefers trying things to reading doc pages, you can type “Plivo” into the Action field to see what actions are available. (Or you can type any string and use any platform that Zapier integrates with.) Complete the form, then click Enable action . At some point you’ll have to specify your Plivo Auth ID and Auth Token to authenticate your account within Zapier. Those are all the steps - sounds easy, no? But some of this software is new and not completely debugged. We had problems connecting our Plivo phone numbers to Zapier through the plugin screen. Also, see the “Have AI guess a value” prompt in the screenshot above? We tried doing that for our source number, since we were using a test account that had only a single active number. AI failed to guess the value. Prompt engineering At this point you’ve created an action that ChatGPT can use by calling the Zapier plugin. Now you have to write a good prompt that not only retrieves the information you want but also lets ChatGPT know what to do with it. We found things worked best when we used a phrase like “send a text using Plivo.” ChatGPT “knew” that it could access Plivo via Zapier, as in this example. When we clicked the link, we found that ChatGPT had filled in the source and destination numbers properly. However, the text we asked it to generate wasn’t what we were looking for; instead of a polite reminder that payment was due, the body of the text was “Recipient’s phone number.” AI works in mysterious ways. There’s clearly a mismatch somewhere in the communication between ChatGPT and Zapier. We took a second try, telling ChatGPT to send the text to a specific destination phone number, but that didn’t help. When we clicked Run , ChatGPT/Zapier/Plivo sent the text perfectly, and it arrived almost instantly, so the good news is that all of the pieces were able to communicate. As if it weren’t enough to automate all it did so far, ChatGPT wasn’t finished. It continued … Sadly, when we clicked on the link, there wasn’t much there but the title of the new Zap. If we had wanted to use it we would have had to fill in all the fields, as if we were starting from scratch. A work in progress From this experience, we judged ChatGPT’s integration with Zapier to be a work in progress - as one might expect for such new software. We wouldn’t rely on it for SMS automation. Still, it’s clear we have a base on which companies can build. Ask us what we think again in six months. The takeaway for now is that you can incorporate ChatGPT into workflows with Plivo - but don’t expect perfection.

title: Pixar, Adobe, Apple, Autodesk, and NVIDIA Form Alliance for OpenUSD to Drive Open Standards for 3D Content
summary: Developers and content creators will be enabled to build an ever-widening range of 3D-enabled products and services.
body_text: Alliance seeks to standardize the 3D ecosystem, advancing capabilities of Open Universal Scene Description (OpenUSD). SAN FRANCISCO – Aug. 1, 2023 – Pixar , Adobe , Apple , Autodesk , and NVIDIA , together with the Joint Development Foundation (JDF), an affiliate of the Linux Foundation, today announced the Alliance for OpenUSD (AOUSD) to promote the standardization, development, evolution, and growth of Pixar’s Universal Scene Description technology. The alliance seeks to standardize the 3D ecosystem by advancing the capabilities of Open Universal Scene Description (OpenUSD). By promoting greater interoperability of 3D tools and data, the alliance will enable developers and content creators to describe, compose, and simulate large-scale 3D projects and build an ever-widening range of 3D-enabled products and services. Created by Pixar Animation Studios, OpenUSD is a high-performance 3D scene description technology that offers robust interoperability across tools, data, and workflows. Already known for its ability to collaboratively capture artistic expression and streamline cinematic content production, OpenUSD’s power and flexibility make it an ideal content platform to embrace the needs of new industries and applications. The alliance will develop written specifications detailing the features of OpenUSD. This will enable greater compatibility and wider adoption, integration, and implementation, and allows inclusion by other standards bodies into their specifications. The Linux Foundation’s JDF was chosen to house the project, as it will enable open, efficient, and effective development of OpenUSD specifications, while providing a path to recognition through the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). AOUSD will also provide the primary forum for the collaborative definition of enhancements to the technology by the greater industry. The alliance invites a broad range of companies and organizations to join and participate in shaping the future of OpenUSD. “Universal Scene Description was invented at Pixar and is the technological foundation of our state-of-the-art animation pipeline,” said Steve May, Chief Technology Officer at Pixar and Chairperson of AOUSD. “OpenUSD is based on years of research and application in Pixar filmmaking. We open-sourced the project in 2016, and the influence of OpenUSD now expands beyond film, visual effects, and animation and into other industries that increasingly rely on 3D data for media interchange. With the announcement of AOUSD, we signal the exciting next step: the continued evolution of OpenUSD as a technology and its position as an international standard.” “At Adobe, we believe in providing artists a set of flexible and powerful solutions running on a variety of devices,” said Guido Quaroni, Senior Director of Engineering, 3D&I at Adobe. “Leveraging a common 3D data representation during the creative process multiplies the value brought by each package and device. OpenUSD was created to be one of these ‘multipliers’ and we are excited to see a diverse group of companies joining together to support this innovative and open technology.” “OpenUSD will help accelerate the next generation of AR experiences, from artistic creation to content delivery, and produce an ever-widening array of spatial computing applications,” said Mike Rockwell, Apple’s vice president of the Vision Products Group. “Apple has been an active contributor to the development of USD, and it is an essential technology for the groundbreaking visionOS platform, as well as the new Reality Composer Pro developer tool. We look forward to fostering its growth into a broadly adopted standard.” “Whether you’re building CG worlds or digital twins or looking ahead to the 3D web, content creators need a cohesive way to collaborate and share data across tools, services, and platforms,” said Gordon Bradley, Fellow, Media & Entertainment, Autodesk. “Autodesk is excited to support the Alliance for OpenUSD as it drives 3D interoperability for visual effects, animation, and beyond, and supports our vision to help customers design and make a better world.” “OpenUSD gives 3D developers, artists, and designers the complete foundation to tackle large-scale industrial, digital content creation, and simulation workloads with broad multi-app interoperability,” said Guy Martin, Director of Open Source and Standards at NVIDIA. “This alliance is a unique opportunity to accelerate OpenUSD collaboration globally by building formal standards across industries and initiatives to realize 3D worlds and industrial digitalization.” AOUSD steering committee members will be speaking at both the Academy Software Foundation’s Open Source Days on Aug. 6 and at the SIGGRAPH conference at the Autodesk Vision Series on Aug. 8 at 1 p.m. PT in Room 404A. To learn more about AOUSD and how to get involved, visit www.aousd.org. To tune into the Academy Software Foundation panel on USD on Aug. 6, 2023, visit the website . About the Joint Development Foundation The Joint Development Foundation (JDF), part of the Linux Foundation Family, provides the corporate and legal infrastructure to enable organizations to develop technical specifications, standards, data sets, and source code. JDF projects such as Ultra Ethernet Consortium, Alliance for Open Media, Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity, and Overture Maps Foundation innovate markets, lead change, and champion open participation and licensing policies. For more information, please visit us at jointdevelopment.org. About the Linux Foundation The Linux Foundation is the world’s leading home for collaboration on open source software, hardware, standards, and data. Linux Foundation projects are critical to the world’s infrastructure including Linux, Kubernetes, Node.js, ONAP, PyTorch, RISC-V, SPDX, OpenChain, and more. The Linux Foundation focuses on leveraging best practices and addressing the needs of contributors, users, and solution providers to create sustainable models for open collaboration. For more information, please visit us at linuxfoundation.org. The Linux Foundation has registered trademarks and uses trademarks. For a list of trademarks of The Linux Foundation, please see its trademark usage page: www.linuxfoundation.org/trademark-usage . Linux is a registered trademark of Linus Torvalds.

title: Can Dogs Eat Sauerkraut?
summary: Can Dogs Eat Sauerkraut? The Potential Benefits and Considerations. Explore Nutritional Value and Safety of Sauerkraut for Canine Consumption.
body_text: As a devoted pet parent, you're no stranger to the questions that arise when considering what foods are safe for your furry companion. One such query that often comes up is whether dogs can enjoy sauerkraut – a tangy and fermented delight that graces many human plates. In this exploration of canine nutrition, we'll delve into the world of sauerkraut, its ingredients, and the factors to consider when deciding whether it's suitable for your four-legged friend. What Is Sauerkraut? Sauerkraut is a traditional dish made from finely shredded cabbage that undergoes a fermentation process. During fermentation, beneficial bacteria naturally present on the cabbage interact with the sugars, transforming them into organic acids. This process imparts the distinctive tangy flavor and unique texture that sauerkraut is known for. Ingredients in Sauerkraut The core ingredient in sauerkraut is cabbage, and some recipes may include additional ingredients like salt. The fermentation process allows for the growth of probiotic bacteria, which not only contribute to the unique taste but also offer potential health benefits. Can Dogs Eat Sauerkraut: A Nutritional Perspective Understanding Canine Diet Dogs are primarily omnivores, which means they can consume a variety of plant and animal-based foods. However, their nutritional requirements differ from those of humans. A balanced canine diet comprises protein, healthy fats, carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals, tailored to their specific needs. The Benefits of Probiotics for Dogs Probiotics, the beneficial bacteria found in fermented foods like sauerkraut, offer potential health benefits. In humans, probiotics contribute to gut health, digestion, and immune system support. Similarly, some experts believe that introducing probiotics into a dog's diet could have similar positive effects on their gut health and overall well-being. Considerations When Feeding Sauerkraut to Dogs While sauerkraut may contain probiotics and beneficial nutrients, there are important factors to consider before offering it to your dog: 1. High Sodium Content: Many sauerkraut recipes involve the addition of salt, which can lead to excessive sodium intake for dogs. High sodium levels can potentially lead to health issues like increased blood pressure and dehydration in canines. 2. Flavor and Preference: Dogs have different taste preferences than humans, and the strong, tangy flavor of sauerkraut may not appeal to all dogs. Some dogs may be more sensitive to certain flavors or textures, making them less likely to enjoy sauerkraut. 3. Potential Gastrointestinal Upset: Introducing a new food to your dog's diet can sometimes lead to gastrointestinal upset. The fermentation process in sauerkraut can result in gas production, which may not sit well with all dogs' digestive systems. 4. Individual Dog's Health Status: Before adding sauerkraut or any new food to your dog's diet, it's crucial to consider their individual health status and any preexisting health conditions they may have. Consulting a veterinarian is advisable, especially if your dog has a sensitive stomach, allergies, or specific dietary needs. Exploring Safe Alternatives Probiotic-Rich Dog-Friendly Options If you're interested in providing probiotics to your dog's diet, there are safer and more suitable alternatives to sauerkraut: Commercial Probiotic Supplements: Many reputable pet food companies offer probiotic supplements specifically designed for dogs. These supplements are formulated to meet your dog's dietary needs while promoting gut health. Plain Yogurt: Plain, unsweetened yogurt is a source of probiotics that some dogs may enjoy. However, it's essential to ensure that your dog is not lactose intolerant before offering yogurt. Fermented Vegetables: If you're keen on incorporating fermented foods, consider offering your dog small amounts of plain, fermented vegetables like carrots or green beans, ensuring they are free from added salts or seasonings. The Final Verdict: Can Dogs Eat Sauerkraut? While sauerkraut does contain potential benefits in the form of probiotics, its high sodium content and potential for digestive upset make it a less suitable option for dogs. Instead, consider exploring safer alternatives that offer the benefits of probiotics without the drawbacks associated with sauerkraut. Promote Your Dog's Optimal Health Prioritizing your dog's nutritional needs ensures a happy and healthy life. While sauerkraut may not be the best choice for canine consumption, there are alternative ways to support their digestive wellness and overall vitality. By making well-informed decisions about your dog's diet, you're contributing to their long-term health and happiness. Want more food tips? Check out " Can You Take Prebiotics and Probiotics Together? title: Fun Family Reunion Ideas & Activities
summary: Discover memorable family reunion ideas and activities for a joyful gathering. Plan the perfect reunion with fun and bonding. ✓ Read here for more.
body_text: Make Memories with These 10 Family Reunion Ideas Every once in a while, it’s crucial to pause the bustle of modern life and take time for family. Family is what grounds us, brings joy, and makes life meaningful. Family reunions hold significance as they reinforce bonds, bridging generational gaps and sustaining familial connections. These gatherings offer a platform to cherish shared histories, stories, and traditions, preserving cultural heritage. They provide a rare opportunity for dispersed family members to interact, nurturing a sense of belonging and mutual support. Reunions are an opportunity for family members to reconnect — or perhaps meet new family members for the first time. So often, family reunions happen around a special event, like a wedding or the holidays. But having time dedicated to only family — not distracted by other priorities — means more quality bonding. Is it time to start planning your family reunion? 10 Fun Family Reunion Ideas Whether your family is big or small, we have whipped up 10 family reunion ideas that all ages will enjoy. Cook Up Memories with Cooking Classes Not sure how to plan a family reunion? Start with a structured activity. If your family is based near New York City, or wants a reason to visit, consider attending a group cooking class taught by top New York chefs! Making and enjoying food is one of the best ways to bond as a family. Learn a culinary skill together, then recreate it at the next reunion. Experiment with a new cuisine, or learn a new way to make an old classic. A CoCuSocial cooking class is a hands-on experience that lasts around two hours. Professional chefs teach attendants how to make dishes like dumplings, tapas, or French pastries. Bring out some friendly competition to see who makes a sushi roll best! Or pretend you’re on a televised cooking show and judge each other’s creations. Most importantly, enjoy a homemade meal or dessert together at the end. Plus, New York is an excellent destination for a family reunion weekend, with much to do once cooking class is over. Bon appétit! Mix it Up with Mixology Classes For those more interested in learning the art of the cocktail, consider a group mixology class when planning a family reunion. Because sometimes, the same old beer and wine selection can get old. Switch it up and learn from the best pro mixologists in town! Plus, if your family has any new 21-year-olds in the house, this is a fun way to welcome them to adulthood. This fun, NYC-based mixology classes offer private instruction for families of up to twenty. All participants partake in their handcrafted concoctions at the end of the class. An Old Fashioned, Mai Tai, or Margarita may become your new specialty if you host the next family reunion. Whether you prefer shaken or stirred, with flavored syrup or a simple garnish, get ready to impress your friends once you nail these refreshing cocktails. Of course, you also apply the techniques you learn to craft mocktails. Cheers! Plan Some Picnic Fun in the Sun Family reunion games, outdoor scenery, and picnic food— this kind of party is always a crowd pleaser. With low cost and low maintenance, a picnic-style family reunion is simple and timeless. When you have an outdoor family reunion, no one has to use their “inside voice” — kids are free to run around. Plus, minimal cleanup is required afterward! First, decide if you would like to host an at-home backyard picnic or opt for an easily accessible spot on the beach, in a public park, or at a scenic overlook. A public place means less pressure on the host. However, popular public places may require reserving a picnic table beforehand. Additionally, make sure bathrooms are accessible for all attendees. And don’t forget to bring sunscreen, bug spray, and plenty of water to all summertime picnics. The casual nature of a family picnic means folks can drop by and leave as time allows. The outdoors puts people at ease, especially with a gentle breeze and beautiful nature to admire. Finger food (like sliders) and picnic games (like cornhole) keep the party going all day. Whether it is catered or everyone packs their food, all generations love a classic family picnic. Connect Digitally with Virtual Classes It is not always possible for family reunion activities to occur in person. Families are often spread out over state lines and time zones, with commitments that make it tough to plan a day that works for everyone. That’s why some families opt for a virtual reunion or virtual component during an in-person reunion. That also accommodates those with travel, health, or mobility concerns. So, what kinds of virtual activities bring people together? Browse virtual cooking classes and see what will entice your family. See something everyone loves to eat, but no one knows how to cook? Learn how to make ravioli from scratch or homemade empanadas over Zoom! Depending upon the chosen cooking lesson, participants will need to gather some basic cooking supplies and ingredients. On the day of the class, set aside a couple of hours for quality instruction, and enjoy the fruits of your labor when finished! Crown the Winner at Game Night Whether your family is playful and silly or fiercely competitive, playing games is a fun way to spend a family reunion. What will be a crowd-pleaser for your family: board games or video games? Perhaps a homemade backyard obstacle course, a card game, or an improv game will forge new bonds and connections. Pick the most inclusive family reunion games for your family’s size and age range. Playing a low-stakes game can lighten the mood and make everyone laugh. Consider factors like time limits and age to find the best games for your group. For large families, choose a game with a round-robin element to ensure everyone participates. Conclude the event with a closing ceremony where you award a fun prize or recognition, like a homemade paper crown signed by all family members. Make it an annual tradition! Explore Nature Together Whether planning an all-day family hike or a simple reunion outdoors, exploring nature together is a low-cost, high-reward way to spend time together. It’s perfect for the no-frills family who doesn’t need anything fancy to have a good time. After all, there’s nothing better than nature’s beauty to put your family in a state of wonder and awe. Gauge your family’s fitness level and plan accordingly. Not all family members will enjoy a high-exertion experience. Consider what is available locally, like parks and recreation departments, nature museums, and state forests. Or seek out a destination reunion, like a favorite beach or mountain lake. Is the weather not cooperating? Take the family to the zoo or an aquarium for an indoor nature experience. Whether your family catches summertime fireflies, picks flowers in the spring, skis in the winter, or loves to walk amongst autumn leaves — nature awaits you. Just be sure to dress accordingly and leave no trace! Unleash Creativity with Arts and Crafts Is your family creative? Creative family reunion themes like arts and crafts give people something tangible to do while reconnecting. Whatever you make will be a memento for years to come, especially when you incorporate the reunion year on the homemade keepsake. Choose a safe craft that all ages can do, or offer a few different ones. For a sentimental activity, decorate picture frames. Set aside time at the reunion to pose for a family photo to put inside the homemade frame. Then sign each other’s frames! For holiday reunions, make Christmas ornaments. Make matching tye-dye family shirts or decorate matching baseball caps for a summertime reunion. Not into matching? Have everyone paint their own birdhouse or individual mug. Some arts and crafts projects are easy to do at home; others are best completed at an art studio. Whatever you make together, it will become a cherished keepsake. Family arts and crafts time will nurture creativity in children and bring out the kid in everyone else. Host the Family Olympics On your marks, get set, go! Get ready to host family reunion outdoor games — Olympics-style. Just as all countries come together in the name of good sportsmanship, all branches of the family tree will reunite for some friendly competition between in-laws. Go all out with opening and closing ceremonies, toy medals, and playing the favorite song of each winner instead of a national anthem. Now, it’s time to choose the games. Select a combination of simplified backyard races or activities — or make up your own games. Opportunities abound to get both creative and athletic when designing your family Olympics. And for those not up for heavy movement, the family Olympics always need announcers, scorekeepers, and cheerleaders! Everyone can get involved, even if they don’t want to exert themselves. Family Olympics may take place over a day, week, or weekend. Ensure everyone stretches, hydrates, and doesn’t get hurt attempting an overly ambitious feat. Document the event with “athlete” interviews, behind-the-scenes training, and other fun videos. Spend Quality Time at Monthly Potluck Parties Who says family get-togethers can only happen once a year? Spend quality time with family every month at a potluck party! When there is no pressure for one person to cook food for everyone, much of the stress of hosting a family reunion is removed. Decide if one person would like to host or if your family would prefer rotating hosting duties between different family members’ homes each month. When family reunions are monthly, there is less pressure to make it perfect. The more quality time you spend together, the more authentic connections form, and the tighter knit you will be as a family. And if someone can’t make it, there’s always next month! Of course, monthly reunions are best for families who live within driving distance of one another. To ensure it all runs smoothly, create a meal signup so that there is an even balance of entrees, desserts, drinks, and sides with no repeat dishes. A potluck with only chips and dip won’t do! That will also ensure that everyone likes at least one dish served. Plan a Family Camping Trip Does your family love the great outdoors? Take a family camping trip somewhere beautiful. Spend a night, weekend, or — for the most in-depth family bonding time — a whole week immersed in nature. Has your family been feeling too tied to technology lately? Unplug and see how it brings the family closer. Eliminate modern distractions and just focus on each other’s company. As you hike, fish, or tell stories around the campfire, generations will learn and laugh with one another. Pick a time of year that suits everyone’s schedules and promises good weather. Alternatively, you can try glamping. Glamping refers to “glamorous camping.” It is the perfect middle ground if your family loves nature but prefers to maintain some comforts of home, like mattresses. Whether you find the ideal glamping accommodations or prefer to rough it the old-fashioned way, camping is a great way to enjoy the beautiful outdoors with family. Plan Your Family Reunion with CoCuSocial Family reunions also create cherished memories, promoting emotional well-being and unity. As life evolves rapidly, these events strengthen relationships, fostering communication, empathy, and understanding.
